subject: biology
title: Biodiversity, pollution and waste
key_idea: **Biodiversity** is the variety of species on Earth or in an ecosystem. High biodiversity keeps ecosystems stable. Human population growth, pollution, deforestation and non-indigenous species reduce it, but human actions can also protect it.

blocks.text: Biodiversity is the variety of all the different species of organisms on Earth, or within an ecosystem. This section covers why a high level is important.

items.meaning: The variety of all the different species of organisms on Earth, or within an ecosystem.
All the living organisms in an area and the physical conditions they depend on.
A species that has been brought to an area where it does not naturally live.

items: A great biodiversity makes an ecosystem more **stable**.
Species depend less on one other species for food, shelter and the maintenance of the physical environment.
A greater diversity of plants gives more different types of food and habitat, so more animal species can live there.
A species can help keep a community stable. For example, a predator controls the population of its prey.
The future of the human species on Earth relies on maintaining a good level of biodiversity.
High biodiversity means a stable ecosystem.
More plant species means more food and habitats, so more animal species.

blocks.text: Rapid growth in the human population and a higher standard of living mean that more resources are used and more waste is produced.
Unless waste and chemicals are properly handled, more pollution is caused. Pollution kills plants and animals, which can reduce biodiversity.

rows: Bacteria multiply and use up oxygen in respiration, so water animals cannot respire. It can also contain pathogens
Causes eutrophication, which lowers the oxygen in the water and kills fish
Kill organisms and can build up in food chains
Animals are trapped or harmed if they swallow it. Most plastics are not biodegradable
Acidic gases damage leaves, so there is less photosynthesis, and they can cause acid rain
Waste takes up land and toxic chemicals harm organisms

diagram.alt: Put the stages of eutrophication in order, from fertiliser run-off to the death of fish.
diagram.prompt: Put eutrophication in the correct order
steps: Fertiliser or sewage is washed into a lake or river, so nitrates build up in the water
Algae grow rapidly, forming an algal bloom
The algae block light, so plants lower in the water cannot photosynthesise and die
Decomposers break down the dead plants and use up oxygen in respiration
The oxygen concentration in the water falls
Fish and other water animals die

blocks.text: Land use, non-indigenous species and overfishing

items: More land is used for farming because the population needs more food. Deforestation, loss of hedgerows and **monocultures** reduce habitats.
Cutting down and burning trees means less photosynthesis, so more carbon dioxide stays in the atmosphere.
Pesticides washed into rivers by rain kill organisms and reduce biodiversity.
A non-indigenous species can **outcompete** native species for food and habitat. It may have no natural herbivores and may carry diseases.
Global warming from extra carbon dioxide and methane changes habitats and migration patterns.
Overfishing reduces fish populations.
Sewage, fertiliser, pesticides, toxic chemicals, plastics and acidic gases all harm organisms.
Eutrophication: nitrates, then algal bloom, then plants die, then oxygen falls, then fish die.
Non-indigenous species outcompete native species.

blocks.text: Humans can also have positive effects. Only recently have measures been taken to try to stop the reduction in biodiversity.

items: Reduce pollution, including the use of pesticides and fertilisers.
Plant trees, and plant a variety of crops instead of a monoculture.
Run breeding programmes for endangered species.
Rewild habitats such as hedgerows and meadows, and leave wider field margins.
Set fishing quotas, avoid catching young fish (for example with larger-holed nets) and protect breeding grounds.
Breed fish in captivity, for example in fish farms, to increase their numbers.
Reducing pollution and restoring habitats increases biodiversity.
Fishing quotas, protected zones and captive breeding help fish populations recover.

blocks.text: Questions often give population data. Work out the change first, then divide.

blocks.label: Mean annual increase
blocks.formula: mean annual increase = (final population − starting population) ÷ number of years
where: populations in the same unit, such as billions

blocks.label: Percentage decrease
blocks.formula: percentage decrease = (starting value − final value) ÷ starting value × 100

diagram.alt: Practice calculating the mean annual increase of a population in millions per year.
diagram.question: The population of a region rose from {start} million to {end} million in {years} years. Calculate the mean annual increase in millions per year, to 2 decimal places.

items: Mean annual increase = change in population ÷ number of years.
Percentage decrease = decrease ÷ starting value × 100.

checks.q: Explain how fertiliser run-off can cause fish in a lake to die.
checks.a: Fertiliser increases the nitrates in the water, so algae grow rapidly and block light. The plants below die and are decomposed by microorganisms, which use up oxygen in respiration. The oxygen concentration falls, so the fish die.

checks.q: In 1900 the human population was 1.6 billion. In 1950 it was 2.5 billion. Calculate the mean annual increase.
Describe two ways to increase biodiversity.
checks.a: Any two from: reduce pollution, plant trees, run breeding programmes for endangered species, rewild habitats or hedgerows, leave wider field margins, plant a variety of crops, reduce the use of pesticides.

more / different types of habitat / shelter or nest sites available

mistakes.wrong: To increase biodiversity, protect habitats and recycle more.
mistakes.right: "Protect or conserve habitats" and "recycling" are ignored. Give a specific action, such as plant trees, rewilding hedgerows, wider field margins, reducing pesticides or reducing pollution.

mistakes.wrong: The fish died because the sewage contained pathogenic bacteria that caused disease.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Explain that bacteria decay the organic matter, respire aerobically and use up oxygen, so the fish have less oxygen and less energy supply.

mistakes.wrong: A prey species is important because it provides food for predators.
mistakes.right: "Provides food" is ignored. Write that it provides energy to the predator.

mistakes.wrong: More trees mean more food available for animals.
mistakes.right: "More food available" is ignored. Write more different types of food, or more different habitats and shelter.

worked_example.question:
A large amount of untreated sewage entered the river. Many fish died. Untreated sewage contains organic matter and bacteria.

Explain why many fish died.
answer_points: Bacteria decay the organic matter in the sewage.
They do this by digestion, for example starch broken down to sugar.
The bacteria respire aerobically, using oxygen.
This lowers the oxygen concentration in the water.
So the fish have a reduced energy supply, which causes their death.
worked_example.tip: Each step must lead to the next, ending with the effect on the fish.

mistakes.wrong: Eutrophication is caused by a build-up of nitrogen in the water.
mistakes.right: "Nitrogen" is ignored. Write that nitrates build up in the water, from fertiliser, run-off or sewage.

mistakes.wrong: Signal crayfish decrease the native crayfish only because they eat them.
mistakes.right: When asked for one other reason, write competition between species for resources, such as food or habitat, or that signal crayfish carry parasites that cause disease in the native population.

mistakes.wrong: Water lilies cover the lake, so biodiversity falls.
mistakes.right: Explain why: less light reaches the water, so less photosynthesis in plants below, and less food for animals. Oxygen concentration also falls.

worked_example.question:
Increased nitrates can cause eutrophication in lakes.

Explain how eutrophication will affect the fish living in the lakes.
answer_points: Nitrates cause an algal bloom, or rapid growth of algae.
The algae and water plants lower in the water are deprived of light, so they die.
The oxygen concentration in the water decreases, due to decomposition.
worked_example.tip: Give three linked steps, ending with the fish dying.

exam_phrases: community is the total number of butterflies in an area
biodiversity takes into account how many different species are present
butterflies depend on buddleia for food
foxes and badgers depend on buddleia for cover
buddleia outcompetes other plants
other plants decrease because they lack light / water / minerals / space
there is less variety of types of butterflies / plants

mistakes.wrong: A large community means a high biodiversity.
mistakes.right: A large community means lots of butterflies. Low biodiversity means they may be of the same or few species.

mistakes.wrong: Buddleia is a pest because it spreads quickly.
mistakes.right: In a six-mark answer, give both a positive and a negative action. Positive: butterflies depend on it for food and foxes and badgers for cover. Negative: it outcompetes other plants, which reduces biodiversity.

mistakes.wrong: A fall from 1.3 million to 400 000 is a percentage decrease of 69.23 %.
mistakes.right: 69.23 is the unrounded working. When the question asks for 2 significant figures, the final answer is 69 %.

worked_example.question:
Buddleia flowers attract butterflies that feed on nectar. Buddleia bushes produce large numbers of very small seeds, so they quickly colonise new habitats. This has resulted in the populations of other plants decreasing. Scientists have noticed there are large communities of butterflies in these areas but the biodiversity of butterflies is low.

Explain how there can be a large community of butterflies but a low biodiversity of butterflies in an area.
answer_points: A community is the total number of butterflies in an area, so there are lots of butterflies.
Biodiversity takes into account how many different species are present, and the butterflies may be of the same or few species.
worked_example.tip: If neither definition is given, lots of butterflies but few species earns one mark.
